reuse.why: Builds on link.findOrCreateBank, handleSyncResponse, bankSync.syncAccount and generalises Pluggy's download into a shared function for Fintegra, but writes clearAccountLink instead of reusing the unlink logic in unlinkAccount.

duplication.why: Collapses four near-identical provider link functions into linkExternalAccount and the upgrade/insert block of all providers into saveLinkedAccount, but clearAccountLink copies unlinkAccount's field reset, the replacedIds loop appears in both branches of saveLinkedAccount, and downloadAkahuTransactions stays a near copy of the new shared download.

placement.why: Link rules live in server/accounts/app.ts and download logic in sync.ts as the tree does; the closed-account check is folded into a helper named for the duplicate-link rule.

scope.why: Everything serves the four steps; the refactor of existing provider link functions is broader than strictly needed but directly supports applying the rules uniformly.

maintainability.why: One validation helper and one save helper used by every provider is easy to own; the mixed-responsibility assertBankAccountNotLinked, boolean sendFileId flag and copied unlink reset are small debts.

bypasses_abstraction.where: clearAccountLink in server/accounts/app.ts re-implements the account reset already inside unlinkAccount instead of extracting and sharing it.

disguised_duplication.where: clearAccountLink (app.ts) is unlinkAccount's db.updateAccount reset under a new name; downloadFileScopedTransactions (sync.ts) is Pluggy's download renamed and parameterised while downloadAkahuTransactions remains a near-identical copy.

abstraction_drift.where: assertBankAccountNotLinked gained replaceExistingLink and an unrelated closed-account branch (step 3/4); saveLinkedAccount gained replacedIds; linkExternalAccount carries a sendFileId boolean flag. GoCardless and EnableBanking keep their own link functions but use the shared assert/save helpers.
